content.title: Browse the catalog landing page and enter a genre listing
content.intent: Prove that `/books` states the total catalog size, lists every genre with its title count, and each genre name links to a genre listing page.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: Equivalence partitioning (`eqp`) and Pagination / sort / filter (`pagination`) via the Search / list profile. This is the baseline catalog-entry journey on `/books`, distinct from genre-list control variations because it exercises the source promises that apply only to the full catalog landing page. Budget ceiling max_pairs=3 retained this highest-value path.

content.title: Request a genre that does not exist

content.technique_notes: Techniques: Negative / error (`negative`) and Pagination / sort / filter (`pagination`) via the Search / list profile. This is a separate negative path because its outcome changes from a valid listing page to an error page with a 404 response. content.title: Browse an existing genre listing with default title order and complete tile metadata
content.intent: Prove that an existing genre listing shows `<total> book(s) found` for all genre matches, defaults to `Title (A-Z)`, and each displayed tile shows a cover image, linked title, author, `Rating: <n>`, and format.
content.technique_notes: Techniques: Equivalence partitioning (`eqp`) and Pagination / sort / filter (`pagination`) via the Search / list profile. Pairwise `covering_array` on the explicit listing controls at strength=2 (risk-judged strength 2 because no money, auth, or data-loss factors apply; effective_t=2, note `strength=2`) produced four sort/show/view combinations. Under max_pairs=3, this retained the default-state valid-genre baseline (`Title (A-Z)` default, `Show` 20, `Grid view`) and evicted the narrower control-variation journeys for rating sort, page-size switching, and layout toggling.
